user.title: Connect to BetterDisplay
user.description: Point Home Assistant at the Mac running BetterDisplay. Turn on the HTTP integration API first, in BetterDisplay under Settings › Integration.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the Mac. A .local name only works if mDNS reaches this Home Assistant instance; if the connection test fails, try the IP address instead.
data_description.port: Port the BetterDisplay HTTP API listens on. Leave at 55777 unless you changed it in BetterDisplay.
data_description.token: Strongly recommended. BetterDisplay listens on every network interface and ships with token authentication turned off, so until you set a token, anything on your LAN can change your monitors. Generate one in BetterDisplay under Settings › Integration and paste it here.

confirm.title: Displays found

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure {title}
reconfigure.description: Update how Home Assistant reaches BetterDisplay. Capabilities are re-probed on save, so use this after moving the Mac to a new address or adding a token.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the Mac. Changing this keeps your existing entities and their history.
data_description.port: Port the BetterDisplay HTTP API listens on. Leave at 55777 unless you changed it in BetterDisplay.
data_description.token: Strongly recommended. Leave empty only if BetterDisplay's token authentication is off, which means any device on your LAN can drive your monitors.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach BetterDisplay. Check that the Mac is awake and on the network, that BetterDisplay is running, and that its integration API is enabled on this port.
error.invalid_auth: BetterDisplay rejected the token. Copy it again from Settings › Integration, or clear the field if token authentication is off.
error.no_displays: BetterDisplay answered but reported no displays. Check that a monitor is connected and awake, then try again.
error.unknown: BetterDisplay returned an unexpected response. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: That host is already set up.

polling.name: Polling
polling.description: How often Home Assistant asks BetterDisplay for the current state of each display.

data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between updates while the Mac is reachable. Every display is read separately, so short intervals mean steady traffic to the Mac; polling automatically slows down while it is unreachable.

input_sources.name: Input sources
input_sources.description: One list per display that supports input switching. BetterDisplay reports all 40 inputs that DDC can address — DVI, VGA, composite and so on — not the ports the panel actually has, so most of them do nothing. Tick only the inputs your monitor really exposes; the rest stay out of the select entity.

wake_on_lan.name: Wake-on-LAN
wake_on_lan.description: Off by default, and worth leaving off: this has not been verified against a sleeping machine, and a Mac on AC power does not sleep at all, so there is usually nothing to wake. Enable it only if your Mac runs on battery and you have confirmed a magic packet actually wakes it.

data.enable_wake_on_lan: Send a magic packet before commands

data_description.enable_wake_on_lan: When on, an unreachable Mac gets a magic packet and the command is retried while it boots its network stack back up.
data_description.mac_address: MAC address of the Mac's active network interface. Wi-Fi and Ethernet have different addresses, and Wake-on-LAN over Wi-Fi is unreliable.

error.invalid_mac: Enter a MAC address as six hex pairs, for example 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e.
